title: NSGo game navigation mesh (version 1)
description: File is a versioned YAML navigation mesh file, such as levels/level1.navmesh.yaml, that a scene names in its navMesh field: the settings it was baked with and one Mesh per agent type.

version.description: Version is the schema version; it must be FormatVersion (1).

settings.description: Settings are the values the meshes were baked with, every field set.

meshes.description: Meshes holds one mesh per agent type, in the order the agent types were baked.

AgentType.description: AgentType is a named kind of agent a navigation mesh is baked for, such as a humanoid or a large creature. A level bakes one mesh per agent type, as Unity's agent types and Godot's per-agent navigation meshes do.

name.description: Name uniquely identifies the agent type, such as "humanoid".

radius.description: Radius is how far the mesh keeps from walls and ledges; 0 uses DefaultAgentRadius.

height.description: Height is the clearance the agent needs; spaces under ceilings lower than it are left out. 0 uses DefaultAgentHeight.

maxSlope.description: MaxSlope is the steepest surface the agent walks on, in degrees from horizontal, below 90; 0 uses DefaultAgentMaxSlope.

maxClimb.description: MaxClimb is the highest step, such as a stair's riser, the agent walks up or down; 0 uses DefaultAgentMaxClimb.

Mesh.description: Mesh is the navigation mesh baked for one agent type: convex polygons over shared vertices, each with triangles that follow the height of the ground under it, plus any point-to-point off-mesh links.

agent.description: Agent is the agent type the mesh was baked for, every field set.

vertices.description: Vertices are the polygons' corners in world space, shared between neighbouring polygons.

polygons.description: Polygons are the mesh's convex walkable polygons.

links.description: Links are optional point-to-point off-mesh connections (jumps, drops, ladders, teleports) applied by NavMesh.

OffMeshLink.description: OffMeshLink is a point-to-point off-mesh connection stored in a baked 3D navigation mesh, such as a jump, drop-down, ladder, or teleporter.

id.description: ID is an optional game-defined link identifier.

start.description: Start is the world-space [x, y, z] entry point of the link.

end.description: End is the world-space [x, y, z] exit point of the link.

radius.description: Radius is the optional endpoint snap and entry tolerance in world units (>= 0).

bidirectional.description: Bidirectional allows traversal from End to Start as well as Start to End when true.

cost.description: Cost overrides the A* traversal cost when positive; 0 uses 3D Euclidean distance.

area.description: Area is the link's navigation area ID (0 for default).

flags.description: Flags holds optional custom link flag bits; world3d.NavLinkOffMesh is always added on load.

userData.description: UserData holds optional game-defined metadata (such as "jump", "ladder", or "teleport").

Polygon.description: Polygon is one convex walkable polygon of a Mesh with its height detail.

vertices.description: Vertices index Mesh.Vertices, from 3 to Settings.MaxVertsPerPoly of them, in order around the polygon.

detail.description: Detail holds the extra vertices sampled on the polygon's edges and inside it where the ground is uneven.

triangles.description: Triangles cover the polygon, winding counter-clockwise seen from above. An index below len(Vertices) names that polygon vertex, and index len(Vertices)+i names Detail[i].

Settings.description: Settings are the voxel resolution and polygon building parameters of a bake, shared by every agent type. A zero field uses its default, and a baked File records every value it was baked with.

cellSize.description: CellSize is the width and depth of one heightfield cell; smaller cells follow the level more closely and take longer to bake. 0 uses DefaultCellSize.

cellHeight.description: CellHeight is the height of one heightfield cell, the precision of heights, clearances and step heights. 0 uses DefaultCellHeight.

minRegionArea.description: MinRegionArea is the smallest area of a connected island of walkable surface that is kept, which drops specks on tables and ledges. 0 uses DefaultMinRegionArea.

maxEdgeLength.description: MaxEdgeLength is the longest a polygon edge along a wall may be before it is split. 0 uses DefaultMaxEdgeLength.

maxSimplificationError.description: MaxSimplificationError is the farthest a simplified wall outline may stray from the walkable area's cell outline. 0 uses DefaultMaxSimplificationError.

maxVertsPerPoly.description: MaxVertsPerPoly is the largest number of vertices in one convex polygon, from 3 to MaxVertsPerPolyLimit. 0 uses DefaultMaxVertsPerPoly.

detailSampleDistance.description: DetailSampleDistance is the spacing of the height samples a polygon's detail triangles follow uneven ground with, at least CellSize. 0 uses DefaultDetailSampleDistance, or CellSize when that is larger.

detailSampleMaxError.description: DetailSampleMaxError is how far the detail triangles may stray from the sampled height before a sample is added. 0 uses DefaultDetailSampleMaxError.

layerMask.description: LayerMask selects the geometry baked: a triangle is baked when its layers share a bit with the mask. 0 uses LayerAll.
